alarms.subject: item:RIMMANDRAKE_DESIGN_KNOCKBACK_FIRST_TOUCH
alarms.why: clause settings_scale_and_switch, inv_settings refused 3 times: criteria repair due

gaps.criterion_why: A scene whose expectation is 'only its own outcome changes' must pin every staged mass that the changed setting reads, or a correct build can fail it; the fix is one assertion.
gaps.observed: The start stages 'a colonist, an animal, a second animal of 100 to 150 kg (asserted: mass read), a mech, a downed pawn'. Only the second animal's mass is pinned. The expect says 'each change alters only its own outcome ... the second animal thrown at default and skipped with reason too_heavy_creature at creatureMassLimit 90'. inv_creature_mass_limit weighs every living pawn, mechs included. So any animal or mech over 90 kg is also skipped at 90, and a correct build reads as a failure. Vanilla masses vary widely, from a 60 kg lancer [measured] to a 144 kg muffalo [stated in sc_mass_and_power].

smallest_fix.what: scenes.json sc_settings_sweep: add a mass assertion under 90 kg to 'an animal' and 'a mech' on the start lane line (or name the extra skips in the expect)

gaps.what: sc_settings_sweep's creatureMassLimit 90 run expects only the second animal to be skipped, but the lane's 'an animal' and 'a mech' have no mass assertion, so a correct build that also skips either one (any of them over 90 kg) fails 'each change alters only its own outcome'
gaps.where: scenes.json sc_settings_sweep: start lane line (245), action (251), expect (252)
gaps.would_pass: Every living pawn in the lane other than the second animal carries an asserted mass band entirely under 90 kg (e.g. 'an animal of 10 to 80 kg (asserted: mass read)', 'a mech under 90 kg, e.g. a lancer at 60 kg (asserted: mass read)'; INVALID otherwise). Or the creatureMassLimit 90 expectation names every lane pawn over 90 kg as skipped too. A script can check that each lane pawn's asserted band lies wholly on one side of 90 kg and under 150 kg.

gaps.criterion_why: A scene's stated mod list must be the list it needs, and the fix itself claims to state the Cauldron's dependencies but states them wrongly.
gaps.observed: Each start line reads 'the Cauldron (mandrake.rm.cauldron) and its dependencies (mandrake.rm.environmentalhazards, mandrake.rm.creaturebehaviors), each asserted active'. src/RimMandrake/Cauldron/About/About.xml lists four modDependencies: brrainz.harmony, mandrake.rm.flowworks, mandrake.rm.environmentalhazards and mandrake.rm.creaturebehaviors [measured]. sc_cover_breaks and sc_gas_shove_into_pit assert FlowWorks in a separate line; sc_gas_chain, sc_cauldron_gas and sc_settings_sweep never name it. RimWorld loads a mod whose dependency is missing with only a warning, so 'Cauldron active' does not imply FlowWorks is loaded [guess ~75%].

smallest_fix.what: scenes.json: add mandrake.rm.flowworks to the Cauldron dependency clause in sc_gas_chain, sc_cauldron_gas, sc_cover_breaks, sc_gas_shove_into_pit and sc_settings_sweep

gaps.what: The Cauldron's dependency list stated in the gas scenes omits mandrake.rm.flowworks, so three scenes state and assert an incomplete list
gaps.where: scenes.json sc_gas_chain, sc_cauldron_gas, sc_settings_sweep start lines (the same wording in sc_cover_breaks and sc_gas_shove_into_pit)
gaps.would_pass: In all five scenes the Cauldron start line names mandrake.rm.flowworks among its dependencies, asserted active, INVALID otherwise. A script comparing each scene's stated Cauldron dependencies with the Cauldron About.xml modDependencies (Harmony excepted) finds no difference.

gaps.criterion_why: An expect that a correct build fails because the staging kills the subject is a staging defect, not a property of the mod.
gaps.observed: The scene stages 'a Bomb explosion ... at radius 2.9 ... and damage 50', then 100, one cell from a 12 kg rat and a colonist. No start line shields them from the blast's injuries. A 50-damage bomb very likely kills a rat, and a 100-damage blast can kill or down a colonist [guess ~75%]. A killed pawn is thrown by the goods rule (sheet.md:33: 'a pawn the blast kills among them, fly wild: about 1.6 times as far'), which breaks the stated cells and 'alive and stunned'. The existing proof's Blast helper (RM_KnockbackProof.cs:588-590) stages damage 1 [measured]: that convention keeps pawns unhurt, but under blastPowerFromDamage (default on) it throws at 1/50 of the force. No scene states the damage it stages.

smallest_fix.what: scenes.json sc_mass_and_power start: add the injury-absorbing hook and its assertion; one line on the staged-damage convention in the prose of RIMMANDRAKE_BUILD_KNOCKBACK_CREATURE_MASS_AND_BLAST_POWER

gaps.what: sc_mass_and_power stages real Bomb damage (50, then 100) one cell from a rat and a colonist, with nothing to keep them alive, yet expects each thrown creature 'alive and stunned' at its kernel cells
gaps.where: scenes.json sc_mass_and_power start (blast line) and expect; tree.json heavier_flies_less
gaps.would_pass: sc_mass_and_power gains a start line: a test hook absorbs the staged explosion's injury on the four creatures (asserted: no new hediff after either run), while the journal's damage ratio is still read from the explosion's damage. The expect keeps 'alive and stunned'. The entry_point_item's prose states that scenes staging a 'grenade' or 'shell' use that projectile's real damage (ratio 1.0), with the same hook wherever survival is expected.

gaps.criterion_why: A leaf's oracle must be what its scene checks, and an asserted start band must not admit states the expect then fails.
gaps.observed: The leaf oracle reads 'the creature mass limit at 250 kg throws the thrumbo (1 then 3 cells)', but the control runs only 'the damage-50 run with creatureMassLimit 250', so the 3-cell result at double damage is never staged. From RM_KnockbackMath.cs ThrowCells (4 x 0.655 x sqrt(70/m), rounded away from zero) [measured from code], a colonist over 76.9 kg throws 2 cells at damage 50, the same as the muffalo. Masses of 77 to 90 kg pass the scene's asserted 'colonist 60 to 90', then fail 'within each run rat > colonist > muffalo > thrumbo'.

smallest_fix.what: scenes.json sc_mass_and_power: add the 250 kg damage-100 control lane (or trim the 'then 3' in tree.json heavier_flies_less), and narrow the colonist band to 60-76 kg

gaps.what: sc_mass_and_power's stated numbers do not match its leaf or its own assertion band: the leaf oracle's thrumbo '1 then 3 cells' is never staged, and the colonist band of 60 to 90 kg lets a correct build fail the strict order
gaps.where: tree.json heavier_flies_less oracle_proposed; scenes.json sc_mass_and_power start (masses), expect, control
gaps.would_pass: Either the control adds the damage-100 run at creatureMassLimit 250, expecting the thrumbo at 3 cells, or the leaf oracle drops 'then 3'. The colonist band reads 60 to 76 kg, so every admitted mass gives 3 cells at damage 50 and 5 at damage 100 by ThrowCells.

gaps.criterion_why: The sweep's rule that each change alters only its own outcome is right; this clause overstates that outcome.
gaps.observed: The expect reads 'the double-damage blast throws each pawn farther than the frag grenade at default'. The lane holds 'a wall behind one colonist, a closed door behind another' and 'a colonist with a charged shield belt'. A wall or door stops a throw dead at the same cell at either damage (sheet.md:29), and an absorbing belt keeps its wearer in place at both (sheet.md:32). 'Each pawn farther' therefore fails on a correct build.

smallest_fix.what: scenes.json sc_settings_sweep expect: replace 'each pawn' with the named free-flying pawns

gaps.what: sc_settings_sweep expects the double-damage blast to throw 'each pawn farther' than the frag grenade, which is false for the lane pawns a wall, a door or a shield belt holds
gaps.would_pass: The clause names the pawns it means: the free-flying colonist, the animal, the second animal and the downed pawn each land farther (or at the cap) at default, with journal damage ratio 2.0, and exactly as far with blastPowerFromDamage off. A script reading the landing cell of each named pawn passes on a correct build.

gaps.criterion_why: The contract's unit rule is clear: every built or in-scope capability is really exercised by a showcase or listed in coverage_rest. The owner asked for 'a single scene', not a showcase that breaks the greedy rule.
gaps.observed: The mass_and_power showcase lists 'inv_who_is_spared' in exercises. record.json:760 defines it as 'body size 2.5 or more, pawns already in a pit, pawns carrying a pawn, flying pawns, pawns in bed or carried'. sc_mass_and_power stages only a rat, a colonist, a muffalo and a thrumbo on open ground, so none of those states. Its one spare, the thrumbo's, is inv_creature_mass_limit's. The leaf's own false_pass (tree.json:118) rejects 'the thrumbo spared by a leftover body-size rule, not by mass'. The contract counts only capabilities a showcase really uses in play, and this one is the third new capability that lifts the showcase to min_new_after_first. The inventory entry still says 'body size 2.5 or more' with no scope_note.

smallest_fix.what: scenes.json: restore the coverage_rest row and drop inv_who_is_spared from mass_and_power exercises, demoting the showcase to a scene if it then has fewer than 3 new; record.json inv_who_is_spared: add the d_mass_limit scope_note

gaps.what: inv_who_is_spared, a built and approved capability, lost its coverage_rest entry and is now claimed only by showcase mass_and_power, whose scene stages none of its states; without it the showcase newly exercises 2 capabilities, under min_new_after_first 3
gaps.where: scenes.json coverage_rest (inv_who_is_spared removed) and showcase mass_and_power exercises; record.json inv_who_is_spared
gaps.would_pass: coverage_rest again holds inv_who_is_spared by ['the_spared', 'sc_spared'], with a why naming its in_pit, carrying_pawn, flying and in_bed lanes, and mass_and_power's exercises drop it. mass_and_power then either stays a showcase with three capabilities it really exercises, or becomes an ordinary scene, with inv_creature_mass_limit and inv_blast_power_damage in coverage_rest by sc_mass_and_power. `designer_stage.py showcases` passes, and record.json inv_who_is_spared carries a scope_note that d_mass_limit replaces its body-size clause.

reasons: The five carried gaps (g1 to g5) look fixed in the entries shown, though none was claimed, and I do not repeat them. The flowworks dependency now matches Cauldron About.xml. sc_mass_and_power has an injury-absorbing hook, the thrumbo at the 250 kg limit is staged at 1 then 3 cells, and the colonist band is 64 to 76 kg. The kernel arithmetic, re-run from RM_KnockbackMath.cs, gives every stated cell count. The thrumbo's 240 kg checks out from its defs (Mass 60 x body size 4) [measured]. The sweep now names only the free-flying pawns as going farther. inv_who_is_spared has its coverage_rest entry back by sc_spared, and the showcase check prints 'showcase set accepted'. One change opens a new gap: the sweep's new creatureMassLimit 90 run pins only the second animal's mass. An unweighed 'animal' or 'mech' over 90 kg would also be skipped and break 'each change alters only its own outcome'. It is a one-line edit to scenes.json, so the verdict is not_covered.
